question:
Select the most appropriate option to complete the given sentence.
The news of his arrest spread rapidly in every _____________ of the city.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. nook and corner.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "nook and corner" means every part or place, without exception; it is used to say that something is present or has spread absolutely everywhere. (हर कोने-कोने में)
◦ Example: The police searched every nook and corner of the house but found nothing.

• In the given sentence, the news of the arrest spread "rapidly in every nook and corner of the city" — that is, it reached the entire city, every part of it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Rack and ruin (बर्बादी की हालत): A state of complete disrepair or ruin, usually due to neglect.
◦ Example: The old palace has gone to rack and ruin for want of care.

• Option 2: Ins and outs (सभी बारीकियां): All the small details of a subject or situation.
◦ Example: She knows the ins and outs of the tax system.

• Option 4: Life and soul (जान): The most lively and entertaining person at a gathering, the one who keeps everyone engaged.
◦ Example: He is the life and soul of every party he attends.

NOTE

• Other common idioms of "everywhere/completeness" asked in SSC: "Far and wide" (over a large area), "High and low" (everywhere, in every possible place) and "Through and through" (completely, in every respect).

question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
A stranger buys flowers for the dead man's grave.
option_1: Flowers is bought by a stranger for the dead man's grave.
option_2: Flowers were bought by a stranger for the dead man's grave.
option_3: Flowers have been bought by a stranger for the dead man's grave.
option_4: Flowers are bought by a stranger for the dead man's grave.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Flowers are bought by a stranger for the dead man's grave.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "A stranger buys flowers for the dead man's grave" is an assertive sentence in the Simple Present Tense (main verb "buys" = V1 + s/es).

• Rule — Simple Present Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + V1/V5 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "flowers" becomes the subject; since "flowers" is plural, the auxiliary used is "are"; the verb "buys" becomes the past participle "bought"; and "a stranger" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: Flowers are bought by a stranger for the dead man's grave.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because the auxiliary "is" does not agree with the plural subject "Flowers"; it should be "are".

• Option 2 is incorrect because "were bought" is the passive form of the Simple Past Tense, not the Simple Present Tense used in the original sentence.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "have been bought" is the passive form of the Present Perfect Tense, not the Simple Present Tense.

NOTE

• Subject-verb agreement is critical while forming the passive of the Simple Present Tense: use "is" with singular subjects, "am" with "I", and "are" with plural subjects or "you".

• The past participle (V3) of "buy" is "bought" — a common irregular verb tested in SSC voice-change questions.

question:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.
He said that he was sorry for all that.
option_1: “I am sorry for all then.” He says.
option_2: “I was sorry for all this.” He said.
option_3: “I am sorry for all that.” He says.
option_4: “I am sorry for all this.” He said.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. "I am sorry for all this." He said.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence is in Indirect (Reported) Speech: "He said that he was sorry for all that." It must be converted back into Direct Speech.

• Rule — Reporting verb: Since there is no listener mentioned (no "told him"), the reporting verb "said" remains "said" in the direct version; it is placed outside the inverted commas exactly as given.

• Rule — Tense inside the quotation: When converting Indirect to Direct, the tense inside the quotation marks is shifted one step forward (un-backshifted). The reported "was sorry" (Past) is converted back to "am sorry" (Present), since the speaker was describing their own present state at the time of speaking.

• Rule — Demonstrative pronouns: While changing Direct to Indirect, "this" becomes "that". Converting back from Indirect to Direct, this change is reversed: "that" becomes "this."
◦ Direct: He said, "I am sorry for all this."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect: it wrongly changes the reporting verb to "says" (should remain "said") and wrongly uses "then" instead of "this."

• Option 2 is incorrect: it keeps the verb inside the quotation as "was sorry" (Past), but Direct Speech reporting the speaker's own present feeling requires "am sorry" (Present).

• Option 3 is incorrect: it wrongly changes the reporting verb to "says" and fails to change "that" to "this" as required when converting back to Direct Speech.

NOTE

• Standard reverse changes when converting Indirect to Direct: that → this, those → these, there → here, then → now, that day → today, the next day → tomorrow, the previous day → yesterday.

• If the indirect sentence uses "told + person", the direct form uses "said to + person" as the reporting verb structure.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
I could not sleep because I was too eager, so I got up early and dressed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Exhilarated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Eager" means keenly enthusiastic, filled with excited anticipation for something. (उत्साहित/उत्सुक)
◦ Example: The children were eager to open their gifts on Christmas morning.

• "Exhilarated" means feeling very happy, excited and full of energy, which is the closest available match in tone and intensity to "eager" in this context — the speaker's excitement was so strong that it kept them from sleeping. (उत्साह से भरा हुआ)
◦ Example: She felt exhilarated after winning the championship.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Apathetic (उदासीन): Showing no interest, enthusiasm or concern; this is nearly opposite in meaning to "eager".

• Option 2: Tensed (तनावग्रस्त): Feeling nervous or anxious; this describes a negative, stressful state, not enthusiastic anticipation.

• Option 3: Satisfied (संतुष्ट): Content or pleased with something already achieved; this does not carry the sense of keen anticipation that "eager" conveys.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "eager" useful for SSC: keen, enthusiastic, avid, zealous, fervent.

• Do not confuse "eager" (looking forward to something with excitement) with "anxious" (worried about something), even though both are sometimes loosely used before "to do something.

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence.
The ruthless story of Pankaj's assassination in the Carribean islands is thrilling to
read.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Carribean.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Caribbean" — relating to the Caribbean Sea and its islands.

• Spelling key: CARI + BB + EAN. Note there is only one "r" (not two) but two "b"s — the exact reverse of what the incorrect spelling "Carribean" (double r, single b) shows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Thrilling" — correctly spelt; means causing great excitement.

• Option 3: "assassination" — correctly spelt; the act of murdering an important person, typically for political reasons.

• Option 4: "ruthless" — correctly spelt; having or showing no pity or compassion.

NOTE

• Commonly confused double-letter spellings tested by SSC: Caribbean, Mediterranean, accommodate, embarrass, occurrence, harass, committee.

• A quick trick: count the letters carefully in words derived from place names, since candidates often swap which consonant is doubled.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The sewage water smells foul.
option_1: Foul is smelt by the sewage water.
option_2: The sewage water is foul when it is smelt.
option_3: The sewage water has a foul smell.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Passive construction is not possible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In "The sewage water smells foul," the verb "smells" is used as a linking (state) verb, followed by the adjective complement "foul" describing the subject — it does not take a direct object.

• Rule: Only sentences with a transitive verb and a direct object can be converted into passive voice, because the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence. Sensory/state verbs like smell, taste, look, feel, sound used to describe a quality of the subject (not to name a substance being sensed) function intransitively and cannot be passivised.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because it wrongly treats "foul" (an adjective/complement, not an object) as if it were an object that can become the subject of a passive sentence.

• Option 2 is incorrect for the same reason, and it also distorts the original meaning of the sentence.

• Option 3 is incorrect because it is merely a rewording of the sentence's meaning using a different verb ("has"), not a grammatically valid passive transformation of the original verb "smells".

NOTE

• Compare: "He smells the flower" (transitive, "flower" is a real object) → CAN be passivised: "The flower is smelled by him." But "The flower smells sweet" (intransitive/linking use) → CANNOT be passivised.

• Other verbs behaving the same way in their state-describing sense: look (She looks tired), feel (The bed feels soft), taste (The soup tastes salty), sound (It sounds strange).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The activist is working really hard and was determined to _________ for this cause.
option_4: keep the wolf from the door
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. move heaven and earth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "move heaven and earth" means to make every possible effort; to try extremely hard to achieve something. (पूरी कोशिश करना/एड़ी-चोटी का ज़ोर लगाना)
◦ Example: The doctors moved heaven and earth to save the patient's life.

• In the sentence, the activist "working really hard and determined" logically fits with making every possible effort for the cause.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Have feet of clay (छिपी हुई कमजोरी होना): To have a hidden weakness or flaw, especially in a person otherwise admired or respected.

• Option 2: Blow his own trumpet (अपनी प्रशंसा खुद करना): To boast about or praise one's own achievements.

• Option 4: Keep the wolf from the door (भुखमरी से बचना): To have just enough money to avoid starvation or serious financial hardship.

NOTE

• Other idioms of effort commonly asked in SSC: "Leave no stone unturned" (to try every possible way), "Burn the midnight oil" (to work/study late into the night), and "Put one's shoulder to the wheel" (to work hard and enthusiastically).

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence.
Being a conscentious and single-minded person, Tubai has become inquisitive and
perseverant in exploring young talents.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. conscentious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "conscientious" — a person who is careful, thorough and diligent, guided by a strong sense of what is right.

• Spelling key: CON + SCI + ENT + IOUS. The word printed in the sentence, "conscentious," is missing the "i" after "consc-" — it should be con-sci-entious, not con-sc-entious.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "inquisitive" — correctly spelt; means eagerly curious, keen to acquire information.

• Option 2: "perseverant" — correctly spelt; means persisting steadily in a course of action despite difficulty.

• Option 4: "exploring" — correctly spelt; means investigating or examining something thoroughly.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "conscientious" (diligent, principled) with "conscious" (aware) — both are frequently tested spelling/vocabulary pairs in SSC exams.

• Other tricky "-tious/-cious/-scious" spellings: ambitious, cautious, gracious, precious, subconscious.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of
words.
A battle or anything involving or causing much bloodshed
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Sanguinary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sanguinary" means a battle or anything involving or causing much bloodshed; bloodthirsty or bloody. (रक्तरंजित/खूनी)
◦ Example: The revolution was marked by several sanguinary battles.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Autocracy (एकतंत्र): A system of government by one person with absolute, unrestricted power.

• Option 3: Ineffable (अवर्णनीय): Too great or extreme to be expressed or described in words.

• Option 4: Redtapism (लालफीताशाही): Excessive bureaucracy or adherence to official rules and formalities, causing delay.

NOTE

• Other one-word substitutes built on "sanguine/sanguinary" family and related bloodshed vocabulary: massacre (indiscriminate killing of many people), carnage (widespread slaughter), belligerent (hostile and aggressive).

• Do not confuse "sanguinary" (bloody) with "sanguine" (cheerfully optimistic) — a common SSC trap.

question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.
In addition to
P. primary threat to the Kemp's ridley sea turtle
Q. capture in fishing gear like shrimp
R. threatened nesting habitat, accidental
S. trawls and gill nets continues to be the
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. RQSP.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Reading the fixed opener "In addition to" together with the parts in the order R-Q-S-P produces a complete, logically coherent sentence: "In addition to threatened nesting habitat, accidental capture in fishing gear like shrimp trawls and gill nets continues to be the primary threat to the Kemp's ridley sea turtle."

• How to identify the sequence: "In addition to" must be followed by a noun phrase naming the first threat — R ("threatened nesting habitat, accidental") — which then needs its noun completed by Q ("capture in fishing gear like shrimp"), since "accidental" (in R) is an adjective that must attach to "capture" (in Q). S ("trawls and gill nets continues to be the") then supplies the main verb "continues to be", and P ("primary threat to the Kemp's ridley sea turtle") completes the sentence as the subject complement.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (SPQR) is incorrect because it places the verb phrase "S" immediately after "In addition to," which is ungrammatical — "In addition to" must be followed by a noun phrase, not a verb.

• Option 2 (SQRP) is incorrect for the same reason — it also starts the sentence with "S" directly after "In addition to."

• Option 4 (PQSR) is incorrect because it produces a meaningless, grammatically broken sequence — "primary threat to the Kemp's ridley sea turtle capture in fishing gear..." does not form a coherent sentence.

NOTE

• In parajumbles, always scan for a grammatical anchor — a preposition, conjunction or fixed opening phrase — and check which part can grammatically follow it; this quickly eliminates wrong options.

• Watch for split noun phrases (like "accidental" needing "capture" to complete its meaning) — parts that must stay adjacent are a strong clue to the correct order.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
The heavy and abundant rainfall has a major role to play in the production of crops.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Ample.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Abundant" means existing or available in large quantities; plentiful. (प्रचुर/पर्याप्त मात्रा में)
◦ Example: The region receives abundant rainfall every monsoon.

• "Ample" means more than enough; sufficient or plentiful, which matches "abundant" in describing a large quantity of rainfall. (पर्याप्त)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Cyclonic (चक्रवाती): Relating to or having the characteristics of a cyclone; describes a type of storm, not quantity.

• Option 2: Intermittent (रुक-रुक कर होने वाला): Occurring at irregular intervals, stopping and starting — this is nearly opposite to the idea of "abundant."

• Option 4: Prolonged (लंबे समय तक चलने वाला): Continuing for a long time — this describes duration, not quantity, and so is not the best match for "abundant."

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "abundant" useful for SSC: plentiful, copious, profuse, bountiful, ample.

• Antonym pairing often tested alongside: abundant ↔ scarce/scanty/meagre.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the
given sentence.
Computers and mobile phones have become a necessary and important part of our
lives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. an essential.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Important" means of great significance or value, and its most natural substitute here is "essential" — meaning absolutely necessary; extremely important. (अनिवार्य/आवश्यक)

• The phrase "an essential part of our lives" is a natural, idiomatic English collocation, correctly paralleling "a necessary ... part" earlier in the sentence: "...have become a necessary and an essential part of our lives."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "a requisite" is incorrect because "requisite" is a formal word normally used to mean a required condition or item (e.g. "a requisite qualification"), and "a requisite part" is an unnatural, awkward collocation here.

• Option 3: "a required" is grammatically weaker and less idiomatic than "essential" in this context; "required" more naturally modifies specific items/conditions rather than describing something's importance to life in general.

• Option 4: "a needed" is similarly awkward — "needed" is rarely used directly before a noun in formal writing in this way, and does not carry the same weight of importance as "essential."

NOTE

• "Essential" and "important" are commonly tested as close synonyms in SSC vocabulary substitution questions.

• Other useful synonyms of "important": vital, crucial, indispensable, significant, fundamental.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
Truth can never be concealed from anyone.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Disguised.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Concealed" means kept hidden or secret; not allowed to be seen or known. (छिपाया हुआ)
◦ Example: He could not conceal his disappointment at the result.

• "Disguised" means given a false or altered appearance in order to hide the truth or one's identity, which, among the given choices, is the closest in meaning to "concealed" — both convey the idea of the truth being hidden or masked from others. (छुपाया/भेस बदलकर छिपाया गया)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Separated (अलग किया गया): Means kept apart or divided; it does not carry the sense of hiding something.

• Option 2: Borrowed (उधार लिया गया): Means taken temporarily with an intention to return; unrelated to hiding.

• Option 4: Snatched (छीना गया): Means taken away suddenly and forcefully; unrelated to hiding or secrecy.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "conceal" useful for SSC: hide, mask, cloak, veil, camouflage, cover up.

• Antonym pairing often tested alongside: conceal ↔ reveal/disclose/expose.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the
given sentence.
He will talk about nothing but films.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. talks about.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes a habitual trait or characteristic of the person — that he only ever talks about films — which is a general truth/habitual action.

• Rule: A habitual action or a permanent characteristic is expressed using the Simple Present Tense (Subject + V1/V5 + Object), not the Future Tense. Since "He" is third person singular, the verb takes "-s": talks.

• The correct preposition to use with "talk" when referring to a topic is "about" (talk about something), so the phrase becomes "He talks about nothing but films."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "was talking at" is incorrect — it wrongly uses the Past Continuous Tense, and the preposition "at" is not used with "talk" to indicate a topic.

• Option 2: "is talking in" is incorrect — the Present Continuous Tense describes an action happening right now, not a habitual trait, and the preposition "in" is wrong; it should be "about."

• Option 3: "shall talking of" is incorrect — it is grammatically broken, as "shall" (a modal/auxiliary) must be followed by a base verb ("talk"), not the "-ing" form ("talking"), without "be" in between.

NOTE

• Habitual/characteristic actions, general truths, and repeated routines are expressed in the Simple Present Tense in English, even when the sentence sounds like it is describing a persistent tendency.

• Common prepositions with "talk": talk about/of (a topic), talk to/with (a person), talk over (discuss in detail).

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that
contains a grammatical error.
She is quiet a generous woman / to have donated / such a large amount / for the flood
affected people.
option_4: She is quiet a generous woman
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. She is quiet a generous woman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the use of "quiet" — the sentence should use "quite" instead.

• Rule — "Quiet" vs "Quite": "Quiet" is an adjective meaning calm, silent, making little noise, whereas "Quite" is an adverb meaning very, completely, to a considerable extent, used to intensify an adjective like "generous" here.

• Since "generous" is an adjective being intensified, the correct word is the adverb "quite": "She is quite a generous woman."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "to have donated" is grammatically correct as used — the perfect infinitive correctly indicates an action completed before the present.

• Option 2: "for the flood affected people." is grammatically correct — it correctly identifies the beneficiaries of the donation.

• Option 3: "such a large amount" is grammatically correct — "such a + adjective + noun" is a standard structure for emphasis.

NOTE

• "Quiet" and "quite" are one of the most commonly confused word-pairs in SSC error-spotting questions — always check whether the word is functioning as an adjective (calm) or an adverb of degree (very).

• Other frequently confused pairs: loose/lose, breath/breathe, effect/affect, later/latter.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
He is diligent, therefore he will _______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. succeed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Diligent" means hardworking, careful and persistent in one's efforts.

• The connector "therefore" signals a logical result/consequence of being diligent. Being hardworking logically leads to success, so "succeed" is the only option that fits the cause-and-effect relationship set up by "therefore."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "remain" is incorrect — it is vague and does not follow logically as a result of diligence; the sentence needs a specific positive outcome.

• Option 3: "fail" is incorrect — this contradicts the logical result of being diligent; a diligent person is expected to succeed, not fail.

• Option 4: "fall" is incorrect for the same reason — it produces an illogical, contradictory result.

NOTE

• When a sentence uses a result connector such as "therefore," "so," "hence," "consequently," the blank must logically follow from the cause stated earlier in the sentence — always check for logical consistency, not just grammatical correctness.

• Related vocabulary: diligent (hardworking) ↔ negligent/lazy (opposite).

question: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. He arrived on Sunday morning.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule — Prepositions of time with days and parts of the day: Normally, "in" is used with parts of the day (in the morning, in the evening). However, when a specific day is mentioned along with a part of the day (e.g., "Sunday morning," "Monday evening"), the preposition "on" is used instead, because the specific day takes priority.
◦ Example: The meeting is scheduled on Friday afternoon.

• Applying the rule: since a specific day ("Sunday") is combined with "morning," the correct preposition is "on": "He arrived on Sunday morning."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "to" is used to indicate direction/destination with verbs of movement, not a point in time.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "at" is used for precise points of time (at 5 o'clock, at noon, at night), not with days.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "in" is used with parts of the day alone (in the morning), months, years and seasons — not when a specific day is attached to the part of the day.

NOTE

• General rule of thumb: "at" for precise time (at 6 pm), "on" for days and dates (on Monday, on 15th August), "in" for longer periods (in May, in 2022, in the morning/evening/afternoon) — but "on" overrides "in" when a specific day and a part of the day are combined.

• Exception to remember: "at night" always uses "at," even though it is a part of the day (e.g., "He arrived at night," but "He arrived on Sunday night").

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given
sentence.
After a prolonged discussion, Gayatri got a permission from her parents to study law.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. got permission.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Permission" is an uncountable (non-count) noun when it refers to the general act of being allowed to do something.

• Rule: Uncountable nouns are not used with the indefinite article "a/an" in their general sense; they can be used without any article, or with a definite article "the" only when referring to a specific, previously identified instance.
◦ Correct: She got permission to leave early.
◦ Incorrect: She got a permission to leave early.

• Since no specific, previously mentioned permission is being referred to, the article-free form "got permission" is correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "got the permission" is incorrect because the definite article "the" wrongly implies a specific permission already known to the reader/listener, which is not the case here.

• Option 2: "got proper permission" is incorrect because it adds the unnecessary and unwarranted qualifier "proper," which changes the meaning of the original sentence rather than simply correcting the grammar.

• Option 4: "got her permission" is incorrect because it changes the meaning entirely — "her permission" would mean permission belonging to/granted by Gayatri, not permission granted to her.

NOTE

• Other common uncountable nouns frequently tested with the same "a/an" error in SSC: advice, information, furniture, news, luggage, knowledge.

• Remember: "a permission" is always incorrect in standard English; use "permission" or "the permission."

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom that can be substituted in
the following sentence.
I begged him to reconsider my application, but he put his foot down.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. refused to yield.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "put his foot down" means to take a firm stand; to refuse to change one's mind or give in to persuasion. (दृढ़तापूर्वक इनकार करना/अड़ जाना)
◦ Example: Her father put his foot down and refused to let her go on the trip.

• In the sentence, despite being begged to reconsider the application, "he" remained firm and did not give in — this matches "refused to yield."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "stamped his foot down" is incorrect — it is a literal, physical action (stomping one's foot), not the idiomatic meaning of firm refusal.

• Option 2: "agreed to reconsider" is incorrect — this is the opposite of the idiom's meaning; the idiom indicates refusal, not agreement.

• Option 4: "did not run" is incorrect — it is an unrelated literal interpretation of "foot" and has nothing to do with taking a firm stand.

NOTE

• Other idioms of firmness/refusal commonly asked in SSC: "Stand one's ground" (to refuse to give way), "Dig in one's heels" (to stubbornly resist), and "Hold one's own" (to maintain one's position against opposition).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Care
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Disregard.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Care" means serious attention or consideration applied to an action; the provision of what is necessary for health, welfare and protection. (देखभाल/ध्यान)

• "Disregard" means to pay no attention to; to treat as unworthy of consideration; a lack of care or attention, which is the direct opposite of "care." (उपेक्षा/अनदेखी)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Concern (चिंता/सरोकार): Means care or interest in something; this is a synonym of "care," not its antonym.

• Option 3: Worry (चिंता): Means to feel anxious about something; it is related to concern/care rather than being its opposite.

• Option 4: Attention (ध्यान): Means notice taken of someone/something; this is also a synonym of "care," not an antonym.

NOTE

• Other antonym pairs of "care" tested in SSC: care ↔ neglect, care ↔ carelessness, care ↔ indifference.

• Be careful in antonym questions to reject options that are actually synonyms of the given word — a very common distractor pattern, as seen with Options 1, 3 and 4 here.

Select the most appropriate answer to fill in blank 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. custom.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "The long-standing (3) custom of child marriage is one of the most prevalent reasons of child marriage." "Custom" means a traditional and widely accepted way of behaving or doing something, practised by a particular group of people over a long period.

• The phrase "long-standing custom" is a natural and commonly used collocation, matching the sense that child marriage is a deeply rooted traditional practice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "taboo" is incorrect — a taboo is a practice that is prohibited or forbidden by social convention, which is the opposite of a widely practised custom; child marriage is described in the passage as being practised, not forbidden.

• Option 3: "faith" is incorrect — "faith" refers to religious belief or trust, not a traditional social practice; "long-standing faith of child marriage" is not a meaningful phrase.

• Option 4: "hassle" is incorrect — "hassle" means an annoying difficulty, which does not fit the meaning of a "long-standing" practice being described as a reason for child marriage.

NOTE

• Recognising fixed collocations such as "long-standing custom/tradition" helps quickly identify the correct word in cloze passages.

• Do not confuse "custom" (a traditional practice) with "customs" (import/export duty) or "costume" (clothing) — commonly confused in vocabulary tests.

solution_text:

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "The elders want to plan for the (4) extension of their family, so they marry off the children to establish their position." "Extension" here refers to the expansion or enlargement of the family, for example through new marital alliances that connect the family to other families and strengthen its social standing.

• This fits the passage's logic: elders marry off children early as a way to expand family ties and secure or strengthen the family's position in society.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "evolution" is incorrect — it refers to gradual development or change over time (often used in a biological or historical sense), not the deliberate expansion of a family through marriage alliances.

• Option 3: "coalition" is incorrect — a coalition is a temporary alliance, typically political, between distinct groups; it does not fit the sense of planning for one's own family here.

• Option 4: "creation" is incorrect — "creation of their family" would suggest the family did not exist before, which contradicts the context of elders already having a family whose position they wish to establish/strengthen.

NOTE

• Cloze passages drawn from informally written source material can contain slightly unusual phrasing; in such cases, choose the option that is most contextually consistent with the surrounding sentences, even if the resulting collocation is not the most common one in standard English.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. obligations.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "Most crucially, poor individuals marry children to get rid of their debts, taxes, dowry, and other (5) obligations." "Obligations" means duties or commitments that a person is legally or morally bound to fulfil, which is the correct general category covering the listed items — debts, taxes and dowry are all types of financial/social obligations.

• The structure "X, Y, Z, and other (5)" requires a word that can serve as a broader category term encompassing "debts, taxes, dowry" — "obligations" fits this role precisely.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "evils" is incorrect — while debts, taxes and dowry may be viewed negatively, "evils" is too broad/moralistic a term and does not specifically capture the shared financial/duty-based nature of debts, taxes and dowry the way "obligations" does.

• Option 2: "activities" is incorrect — debts, taxes and dowry are not "activities" (actions being done); they are financial burdens/commitments, which "obligations" captures accurately.

• Option 4: "mitigations" is incorrect — "mitigations" means actions taken to reduce the severity of something, which does not fit as a category alongside "debts, taxes, dowry."

NOTE

• When a cloze blank follows a list (e.g., "X, Y, Z, and other ___"), look for a word that acts as an umbrella term covering all the listed items — this is a very common and reliable strategy in SSC cloze passages.
